Satisfactory is a fantastic game that I have invested 300 hours in, and counting. The game's unique take on the factory-building genre, set in a sci-fi world, provides a refreshing experience that is both challenging and rewarding. The graphics are stunning, with a beautiful and immersive environment that is constantly being updated.

The gameplay is smooth and enjoyable, with the ability to control multiple drones to automate your factories and manage resources. The game's constant updates keep it fresh and exciting, with new features and improvements added regularly. The community is supportive and helpful, making it easy to connect with other players and enjoy the game together.

Despite the occasional lag or bug with the most recent update, the developers are quick to address and fix any issues, which is greatly appreciated. The game's multiplayer aspect is also a plus, allowing players to collaborate and build huge factories together. The in-game economy is well-balanced and the progression system is well thought-out, providing a sense of accomplishment as you advance.

Overall, Satisfactory is a fantastic game that I highly recommend to anyone who enjoys factory-building games, sci-fi, or simply enjoys a challenging and rewarding experience. With its constant updates and improvements, this game will keep you entertained for hours on end.

This game has the same creative do-whatever-you-want aspect that any open-world sandbox game provides. The world is absolutely massive and stunning with extreme amounts of detail poured into every rock and tree. As you gradually grow your factory you learn new and better ways to do things and rebuild to match your factory's needs. Aside from the factories themselves there is an enormous amount of freedom when it comes to designing buildings, towers, bridges, tunnels, you name it. As I'm writing this review I have over 1000 hours of time in game and I'm not even close to being done with my first play through. I know plenty of people feel they've reached the end after only 40 or so hours, so don't feel like you have to commit all your time. The development team behind this game is the best of any game I've ever played. They interact with the community on a weekly basis and are extremely receptive of community feedback. (not to mention they have a killer sense of humor) I recommend this game to everyone, even you, yes I'm talking to you.

My third time updating this review over the past 2 years: The game is still getting amazing updates and continuing to be just plain awesome.

⭐⭐🔵🔵🔵 2/5: Meme-y Automation Game 
I can't really get myself to like this after experiencing what Factorio does. It's definitely a game, but its extreme reliance on loading bars to craft is making it severely annoying. In Factorio my character crafts in the background while I can still work on the Factory and that right from the start. In Satisfactory I have to first craft by holding the left mouse button for half an hour before any reasonable automation is present.

There is a lot to love about Satisfactory. There is no artificial difficulty: you get all of your resources refunded when deconstructing anything, hostile mobs only target you and not your factories, no survival mechanics. The difficulty lies in the organizational aspect of how to layout and incorporate new machinery to your builds. The assembly line gets very complicated, so don't be afraid to deconstruct your current spaghetti of belts entirely if need be (even if your inventory is full, resources drop into boxes in place of where they stood). This game will have you sit and think about how you're going to ramp up production, plan new factories, or manage resource transportation for quite some time, so I'd recommend this for people who like logic based puzzles. Beginner tip: when crafting parts manually, you don't need to hold space, just tap it and it will craft automatically.

This is a amazing game, and I would like to share my thoughts and feelings about it.
There is no reason for why I even play this game, may it be for fun, or just out of bordem. This game feels more like a chore, you gotta do this, but you don't want to! But eventually, the time will come when you do it, so you can either fix your machines now, even though you don't want to, or not do it now, but still do it later. Eventually, you will have to do it. You will have to study. You will have to do the dishes. You will have to file your taxes. You will have to get your drivers license. You will have to pay for this, pay for that. You will have to go to the shops. Eventually, it will happen. Theres no stopping it. This is a great game, if you are lazy, you will walk 3 steps and get bored. If you are willing to work, you will build your empire. One of the best games I have ever played.
